name: Differentiable Rasterization via Ray Casting
definition: A differentiable rasterization technique that converts a mesh (vertices and faces) into a 3D voxel volume by casting random rays from each voxel center to a random point on the top plane of the bounding box. It computes the forward pass (voxel occupancy) and backward pass (gradients w.r.t. vertex positions) to enable gradient-based optimization of mesh geometry from voxel supervision.
summary: Differentiable Rasterization via Ray Casting converts triangle meshes to voxel volumes using deterministic ray casting and specialized geometric gradient approximation for backward passes.
